question: Fee census of the long tail: transcribe published DAF admin fees (rate tiers, minimum annual fee, opening minimum, gift/grant fees) for a stratified sample of about 60 of the 641 DAFRC community foundations with < $50m of FY2024 DAF assets (strata $10-50m / $1-10m / < $1m, and by CF vendor family), with robots.txt checks and the same fee engine and quote verification as scripts/mission_cf_fee_census.py
conclusion_affected: Whether tail sponsors charge more or less than the top-100 CF median (100/100/67 bps) and the nationals (60/45 bps); the price headroom for an AI-native platform serving the tail
rationale: No sponsor below $50m has a fee row in the repository: cf-daf-fee-census-2026.csv stops at the 100th CF ($101.4m) and sponsor-fee-schedules.csv covers 11 nationals, all above $50m. The tail is 1,240 of 1,514 FY2024 sponsors (81.9%), and 641 of them are CFs, so the fee gap is the largest unknown in the tail profile. Minimum annual fees ($50-$2,500 in the top-100 CFs) dominate the effective rate at the tail's median account of about $133k

question: Operating cost per DAF dollar and per account in the long tail: join the already-harvested FY2022-25 Form 990 Part IX lines (IT, management and other fees, total functional expenses, staff counts) in form990-returns-schedule-d-harvest-full.csv to the 1,240 sponsors < $50m, separately for CFs (where DAFs are one fund type among several) and single-issue sponsors, and compare with the top 50; report the cost that DAF administration plausibly carries per account [I-labelled allocation]
conclusion_affected: The size of the back-office cost pool an AI-native administrator could replace or reduce in the tail (inference in direction-long-tail-sponsors.md §5)
rationale: The tail holds 2.8% of FY2024 corrected DAF assets but its median sponsor runs 24 accounts averaging $133k, so fixed costs per account are likely high; 351 of 641 tail CFs show a Foundant/akoyaGO/other vendor on their site, but nothing in the repo measures what administration costs them. The Part IX fields are already parsed for every DAFRC sponsor, so effort is low

question: Persistent low payout in the long tail: for the 165 sponsors < $50m whose DAF payout (grants / prior-year assets) was below 5% in each of FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024 ($0.72bn of FY2024 assets; 83 CFs, 37 other single-issue, 29 university/hospital, 15 religious), read the latest 990 Schedule D Part I and Schedule O / narrative to separate dormant DAFs, endowed or designated funds reported in the DAF column, and timing artefacts; check whether any sponsor states an inactivity or minimum-distribution policy
conclusion_affected: Whether the tail's 26.8% share of sponsors under 5% payout (0% in the top 50) is real dormancy or a classification effect; the size of the 'activation' opportunity named as inference in direction-long-tail-sponsors.md §5
rationale: Tail payout is bimodal: FY2024 median 11.7% but 26.8% of sponsors below 5% and 7.7% at zero or below, rising to 37.6% and 15.9% under $1m. Sponsors that fall into persistent low payout are also those most often flagged as reporting gaps in tier-b-daf-exit-reasons.csv, so the low-payout set may overlap with misreported Schedule D lines
